newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS FACE INJURY WORRY OVER GIBBS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS FACE INJURY WORRY OVER GIBBS.

text.p: Centre Scott Gibbs' future on the British Lions tour looked in jeopardy after he was stretchered off during the 18-14 win over Border on Wednesday.
Lions manager Fran Cotton said Gibbs would have X-rays on his ankle for suspected ligament damage.
"Scott will fly down to Cape Town first thing in the morning ahead of the rest of us and his first stop will be to have an X-ray at hospital," Cotton said.
"At the moment not even our doctor knows the extent of the damage and until we do we can say no more at the moment."
Scrum-half Austin Healey was also taken off as a precaution after damaging a shoulder in a game played in atrociously wet and muddy conditions.
The Lions' management put on a brave face after the victory which was secured only by a Rob Wainwright try with seven minutes remaining.
"Out of 14 teams in South Africa, Border are probably ranked about 11th so you could say that the Lions have some work to do," said Border coach Ian Snook.
Border hooker and captain Ruhan van Zyl echoed criticisms of the Lions tight five made by Eastern Province at the weekend.
"I didn't think they were as strong as we thought they would be. We expected a lot more from them," said van Zyl.
"I feel they are vulnerable upfront, they weren't great in the scrums and I think they will really struggle in the tests."

Cotton said: "The South African press were expecting us to beat Border pretty convincingly but sometimes you need a sharp reminder that things don't come easy on tour -- especially in South Africa and in these very difficult conditions.
"In my own experience I can only remember worse conditions on about two occasions."
Lions coach Ian McGeechan was more upbeat. "We scored three tries to one with a new team that has had to perform in very difficult conditions.
"You have to remember that this team was an unknown quantity but in the last 15 minutes it was all Lions."

Try scoring wing John Bentley, playing his first rugby union international in nine years since returning from rugby league, said: "It was a great honour and beyond my wildest dreams until a couple of weeks ago.
"At the end of the day when we look back at the fixture column we'll see a 'W' in the right hand column which is all that matters."
The Lions are next in action against Western Province in Cape Town on Saturday.
